segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: First of all, we would like to express our deepest appreciation and gratitude

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: to our legislators present here, led by Senior Vice Chair Garcia

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Congresswoman Garcia, Congressman Arrogancia, Congresswoman Lagdameo,

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Congressman Fuentebella, Congresswoman Bondoc, and Congresswoman Suansing.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: And to all our CSO representatives here present, again, marami pong salamat.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: As we conclude today's People's Budget Review, allow me to begin with a very familiar story.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: The story of the blind man and the elephant.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Each man touched a different part of the elephant.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: One touched the trunk and said the elephant was like a snake.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Another touched the leg and said it was like a tree.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Another touched the side and said it was like a wall.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: It was describing something real, but none, by himself, had the complete picture.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: In many ways, this is also true of the national budget.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Government agencies see it from the perspective of programs and implementation.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Economic managers see it from the perspective of fiscal discipline and national priorities.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Congress sees it through its constitutional power of the purse

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: and its responsibility to represent the people.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Researchers examine the numbers and evidence

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: and CSOs and people's organizations see how government policies and programs are actually

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Each perspective is important, but no single perspective gives us the whole picture.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: This is why evidence-based budgeting is so important.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: When Congress decides how trillions of pesos of public resources should be allocated, we

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: should be able to answer some very basic questions.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: What problems are we trying to solve?

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: What has the government already spent on?

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: And what should we do differently?

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: answer these questions is often fragmented across agencies and information systems.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: We have financial information on how much has been obligated and disbursed, but information

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: on what government actually delivered and what outcomes those expenditures produced

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: is not always as readily available, timely, or comparable.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: This points to the need for a more systematic approach to evidence gathering

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Such a system should identify a core set of critical performance indicators that every

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: government agency is required to regularly report and publish.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: These indicators should allow us to follow the entire results chain, from inputs and

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: and ultimately to outcomes and impacts.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: And this information should not remain scattered among individual agencies or buried in periodic

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: We need an integrated data system that allows Congress, government decision makers, CSOs,

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: researchers, and ultimately the public to have real-time or near-real-time

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: access to financial and performance information, especially given this age of

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Imagine how this change could change budget deliberation.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Instead of asking how much did we appropriate or how much was spent, Congress could ask

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: what did we accomplish and what we spent.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: This is the kind of evidence base we need for better budgeting.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: But even the best government information system cannot tell us everything.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Official indicators tell us what numbers show.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Citizens and civil society can help tell us what those numbers mean on the ground.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: This is where CSOs and people's organizations become indispensable.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: For legislators, civil society provides an important independent source of information

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: CSOs can tell us whether services actually reach intended beneficiaries, whether a program

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: that appears successful in an agency report is working in communities, and whether important

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: They help Congress see another part of the elephant.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: This is why the House of Representatives has taken steps to widen people's participation

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: We have established mechanisms for CSO accreditation and participation in agency budget hearings,

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: provided opportunities for the submission of position papers and recommendations, undertaken

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: budget literacy activities, expanded access to budget information, and created opportunities

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: such as today's dialogue for civil society to engage directly with legislators.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: But we must also recognize that participation remains a work in progress.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Are we hearing from a sufficiently broad range of organizations, including those outside

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Metro Manila and those representing marginalized communities? Do CSOs have the technical capacity

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: and information needed to participate effectively?

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Are budget documents provided early enough and in forms that can be readily

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: And perhaps the most important question is whether participation actually influences

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Moving forward, therefore, I believe we need to pursue two mutually reinforcing reforms.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: First, we need a stronger evidence infrastructure, a unified monitoring and evaluation system,

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Interoperable information systems and real-time or near real-time access to financial and

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Second, we need stronger participatory institutions, earlier engagements of CSOs, better access

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: to information, stronger budget literacy, clearer channels between CSOs and legislators,

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: and mechanisms for tracking how civil society recommendations are considered in the budget process.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Better data without participation can give us numbers without sufficient context.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Participation with good data can give us perspectives without sufficient evidence. We need both.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: And this brings us back to the blind man and the elephant.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: The objective is not merely to bring more people around the elephant.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: It is to ensure that it brings evidence from the part that he or she can see.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: And that's what we put all of that together to put the evidence into an understandable whole.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: That, I believe, is what a truly evidence-based and participatory budget process should accomplish.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Thus, on behalf of the Congressional Policy and Budget Research Department,

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: I thank our members of Congress, our CSOs, PO partners, and everyone who participated in today's dialogue.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: May what we heard today find its way into our continuing budget deliberations,

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: our oversight work, and our efforts to further institutionalize meaningful participation in Congress.

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: Because ultimately, a people's budget should not only be a budget for the people,

segments.speaker: CPBRD Deputy Secretary General Dr. Romulo Emmanuel Miral Jr.
segments.text: it should be a budget informed by evidence, accountable for results, and increasingly shaped with the people. Maraming salamat po at magandang hapon sa ating lahat.
